scope: Proposition 3.6 (Uniform single-well eigenvalue oracle) of the manuscript “Continuum Coulomb hardness with binary nuclear charges” (preprints/Continuum-Coulomb-hardness-with-binary-nuclear-charges-September-24-2026/Continuum-Coulomb-hardness-with-binary-nuclear-charges-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 275 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 290f40f845dc3e0d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 21. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Suppose the centers and the parameters in [1, 4]m are rational, and all their numerators and denominators, as well as those of q, q′, have at most B bits. Under the hypotheses of this section, a deterministic algorithm returns rational numbers ℓi ≤ λi ≤ ui with ui − ℓi ≤ εD, εD = 2−⌈8D/5⌉ < e−1.1D . (3.32) Its bit complexity is polynomial in D, m, B. The bound is uniform over every rational sample in [1, 4]m; no spectral gap of a Ritz matrix is assumed.
